outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms are expected today across the central Gulf Coast states, where tornadoes, wind damage and isolated large hail will be likely with the strongest of storms. Storms with large hail and wind damage may also occur further north across the Ohio and Tennessee Valley, some of which could have very large hail.

sections.title: Southeast
sections.text: A progressive upper-level trough will move quickly east-northeastward from the southern Plains into the Arklatex and Ozarks today, as a 60 to 80 knot mid-level jet translates northeastward from the lower Mississippi Valley into the Tennessee Valley. At the surface, a warm front will move northeastward across the central Gulf Coast States. This warm front will be an important player for the severe threat. To the southwest of the warm front, surface dewpoints will be in the 60s F, contributing to a broad warm sector with moderate instability. Thunderstorms associated with a substantial severe threat, will be ongoing at the start of the period from central Mississippi south-southwestward into southeastern Louisiana. These storms will move northeastward across the central Gulf coast states during the morning into early afternoon. A low-level jet should be positioned over southern Mississippi at daybreak with the jet moving northeastward into central Alabama by midday. This feature combined with the mid-level jet will create strong deep-layer shear favorable for supercells. sections.title: Ohio and Tennessee Valleys
sections.text: An upper-level low will track eastward across the lower Missouri Valley today as the left exit region of a 60 to 80 knot mid-level jet moves across the Ohio Valley. At the surface, a 1000 mb low will track east-northeastward across the mid Mississippi Valley. A narrow corridor of maximized low-level moisture will be in place from western Tennessee into southern Missouri, where surface dewpoints will be in the 50s F by late morning. Scattered thunderstorms are expected to form from this corridor eastward into the lower Ohio Valley this afternoon, where 700-500 mb lapse rates will be steep and large-scale ascent will be strong. This should be favorable for relatively low-topped supercells with isolated large hail. A few of the storms could produce hailstones of greater than 2 inches in diameter. An isolated wind-damage threat could also develop with the stronger supercells. The area with the greatest threat for very large hail will be from far southeast Missouri northeastward across western Kentucky and into far southern Indiana. In this area, lift associated with the mid-level jet, instability and mid-level lapse rates will be most favorable. ..Broyles/Squitieri.. 03/18/2022

outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms are most likely through this afternoon across portions of the Southeast States where a few tornadoes, damaging winds, and large hail are possible.

sections.title: Southeast
sections.text: Broad MCS with an embedded QLCS should continue to move east from AL and southeast MS into GA and the FL Panhandle through this afternoon. This activity has been supported by persistent warm theta-e advection from the central Gulf Coast, with much of it remaining elevated above a surface stable layer. The surface-based warm sector characterized by mid 60s dew points should spread northeast across the southern AL into southwest GA. With some boundary-layer heating along the leading edge of this richer moisture, an increase in severe potential may be realized within the southern extent of convective development prior to hodograph curvature shrinking as low-level flow becomes veered from the southwest. Scattered damaging winds and a few tornadoes are the most likely hazards. Overall severe threat should wane this evening as large-scale ascent diminishes during the late afternoon.

sections.title: Mid-MS to OH/TN Valleys
sections.text: Primary forcing for ascent into this afternoon will be tied to the mid-level trough and attendant surface cyclone gradually shifting from the Ozark Plateau towards the Saint Louis area. Arcs of lower-topped convection are anticipated along the northern periphery of weak surface-based buoyancy. 30-40 kt effective bulk shear in addition to some elongation of hodographs should support a few supercells with mid-level updraft rotation and severe hail as the primary hazard. A couple tornadoes remain possible, particularly near the Lower OH Valley portion of the threat area, where modest low-level hodograph curvature may be maintained near the apex of mid to upper 50s surface dew points. Farther south, a more conditional severe threat is anticipated in the wake of the large MCS across the Deep South. Mid-level subsidence and drying is indicated by most guidance and updrafts will probably struggle along the cold front sweeping east to the south of the MO cyclone. Guidance may be somewhat overdone with the degree of boundary-layer moisture return given just how extensive convective overturning has been this morning in MS to western TN/AL. outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms are expected through the afternoon and early evening across portions of the Southeast States where a few tornadoes and damaging winds are possible.

sections.title: Middle Gulf Coast/Southeast States
sections.text: A nearly continuous squall line extends at midday from west-central Georgia and southeast Alabama, where it is been elevated this morning, southwestward into far south-central Alabama and the far western Florida Panhandle. This southwestern-most portion is where somewhat more broken bands of storms exists and more buoyant surface-based conducive air resides coincident with dewpoints in the upper 60s/near 70F. Heights will tend to rise this afternoon as the richer low-level moisture otherwise advects east-northeastward toward southeast Alabama/southwest Georgia. Low-level winds will tend to further veer and modestly weaken, but nonetheless remain sufficiently strong for well-organized and rotating storms, which include a tornado and damaging wind risk.

sections.title: Middle Mississippi to Ohio/Tennessee Valleys
sections.text: The main forcing for ascent through afternoon will be related to the northeastward-transition of the mid/upper-level low over the Ozarks at late morning. Although only modest cloud breaks are noted at midday, relatively cool mid-level temperatures in conjunction with 50s F dewpoints will be sufficient for modest surface-based destabilization this afternoon. Arcs of low-topped convection are anticipated along the northern periphery of this weak surface-based buoyancy. 30-40 kt effective bulk shear in addition to some elongation of hodographs should support a few supercells with mid-level updraft rotation and severe hail as the primary hazard. A tornado or two may also occur, particularly near the Lower Ohio Valley portion of the severe risk area. mesoscale_discussions.summary: An isolated severe wind and tornado threat should continue with storms moving eastward this morning. Downstream watch issuance is being considered.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A bowing line is progressing fairly quickly eastward across parts of southern/central AL this morning, aided by strong low-level warm advection associated with a 45-55 kt southerly low-level jet. Most of the line remains elevated as of 1215Z, with a continued lack of recent severe/damaging wind reports. Current expectations are for the southern part of the line (across mainly southern AL), and any discrete cells that can form ahead of it, to have the best potential for severe in the short term. Strong low-level shear remains favorable for updraft rotation, and any storms that can become surface based may pose a threat for tornadoes in addition to damaging winds. The main limiting factor still appears to be that the fast eastward progress of the ongoing convection is generally outpacing the more substantial low-level moisture return. Still, a couple of confluence bands have recently developed ahead of the line across far southern MS into coastal southern AL. This area should have the best chance for severe storms this morning as surface dewpoints increase into the mid to upper 60s. A downstream Tornado Watch is being considered for more of southern AL and parts of the western FL Panhandle.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Tornadoes remain possible across a small part of southern Alabama into the western Florida Panhandle.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Strong storms currently exist just north of Mobile AL, within a line extending northeastward toward the larger-scale MCS over eastern AL. Surface observations show rapidly increasing low-level moisture just ahead of the southern cluster near Mobile, where additional warm advection cells are forming and feeding into this developing mesoscale system. Further, visible imagery shows filtered sunshine downstream into the FL Panhandle, which may accelerate eventual mixing and moisture advection northward ahead of the developing complex across southern AL. Given 0-1 SRH of 200-300 m2/s2 and mesoscale lifting, a tornado, possibly strong, may form over the next few hours, in an area bounded to the north by the MCS outflow, and to the east by the relatively drier air. ..Jewell.. 03/18/2022 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe wind gusts or perhaps a couple tornadoes may occur east of tornado watch 51, and and a new watch appears likely.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Outflow with a line of storms continues to surge southward across southeast AL and into southwest GA. While this may result in lower tornado probabilities due to undercutting outflow, the air mass is gradually destabilizing ahead of it. Therefore, an uptick in damaging wind potential may materialize later today. Farther west into south-central AL and western parts of the FL Panhandle, better separation from the outflow to the north, combined with strong shear and higher dewpoints still suggests a tornado or is possible. Storms south of the main outflow boundary may also briefly acquire rotation as the intercept the boundary due to enhanced lift.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Cold temperatures aloft will support marginally severe hail with discrete convection along the warm front. Some intensification may occur later this afternoon with a modestly warming and moistening boundary layer. Current trends suggest a watch is unlikely, however.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Modest convective activity continues along the cold front in north-central Arkansas into parts of southern Missouri. A couple of discrete thunderstorms have developed in north-central Arkansas over the last couple of hours and have become briefly more intense on KSGF radar imagery. MRMS MESH data has shown brief pulses to 1 inch hail as well. Given the cold temperatures aloft in proximity to the upper low and the steep mid-level lapse rates observed on the LZK and SGF morning soundings, it is reasonable that these storms could produce very isolated, marginally severe hail. The limiting factor will be very low buoyancy. Objectively mesoanalysis shows only around 250-500 J/kg MUCAPE. A narrow cloud break is noted just ahead of the Arkansas activity. Modest surface heating and downstream dewpoints creeping into the mid 50s may support intensification later this afternoon. Currently, however, the overall threat appears too marginal for a weather watch.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A few strong to severe wind gusts are expected as activity continues east across southern Georgia. Isolated severe remains possible into the Florida Panhandle.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Numerous storms extend along multiple gust fronts from the FL Panhandle into southern AL and GA, become mostly parallel to winds aloft. An exception has been a more north/south oriented line moving across southwest GA, and this complex has recently produced a measured 52 KT gust at KBGE. Northern portions of this particular bow are elevated, with smaller gusts magnitudes measured as a result of being north of a stabilizing outflow boundary. While low-level moisture slowly increases, warming temperatures will lead to favorable low-level lapse rates which may further enhanced gust potential. A narrow corridor across southern GA, ahead of the converging outflows, appears to contain the greatest risk for severe gusts over the next few hours. Farther west across the FL Panhandle, most of the activity is becoming elevated as cells move across the east-west oriented boundary. While this boundary continues to move south as well, a brief tornado or wind gust may occur as storms intersect it as 0-1 km SRH remains over 200 m2/s2. ..Jewell.. 03/18/2022 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorm intensity has modestly increased within the Missouri Bootheel Vicinity. Signs of destabilization are also evident in western Tennessee. The strongest storms may produce large hail and isolated wind damage. A tornado is possible near the warm front. A watch is possible depending on storm coverage and intensity trends this afternoon.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Visible satellite trends near and ahead of the advancing cold front show a modest increase in vertical motion. This is most obvious along the western flank of stable stratiform clouds in western Tennessee and Kentucky. Dewpoints in these areas have steadily risen during the day to the mid 50s F in parts of southern Kentucky to upper 50s F in western Tennessee. This has supported a recent uptick in storm intensity across the Missouri Bootheel vicinity where 1 inch hail has recently been reported. Over the next 2-3 hours, additional heating may promote 500-750 J/kg MLCAPE across the region. With cold temperatures aloft and 35-45 kts of effective shear, discrete storms would be capable of large hail and isolated wind damage. Surface winds ahead of the front have had some tendency to veer with the greatest pressure falls being analyzed in eastern Kentucky and southern Ohio. However, VAD winds in the vicinity of the warm front still show sufficient low-level turning for a tornado or two with the strongest convection. Current observational trends would suggest a greater severe threat may not materialize for another couple of hours, depending on the degree of destabilization. Given the uncertainty, watch issuance is uncertain but possible. Trends will continue to be monitored this afternoon.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The threat for isolated damaging wind gusts and/or a brief tornado may continue past 23Z. An extension in time may needed to be considered for portions of Tornado Watch 52.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A line of thunderstorms continues to move eastward across the central FL Panhandle and adjacent parts of far southwest GA. Northern portion of this line has recently shown more forward propagation than areas farther south. Storm motion within the northern portion of the line is estimated at 40 kt, bringing it to the edge of Tornado Watch 52 soon. This portion of the line is likely elevated behind the surface front and continues to move eastward into a less favorable thermodynamic environment. More southerly/westerly portion of the line is moving considerable slower, with recent storm motion estimated at 25 kt. Some acceleration may occur as this portion of the line interacts with the southward moving outflow. Even so, thunderstorms will likely persist across the central FL Peninsula past the watch expiration time of 23Z. Environmental conditions will continue to support isolated damaging wind gusts and a brief tornado or two, so an extension in time may needed to be considered for Tornado Watch 52. ..Mosier.. 03/18/2022 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: At least isolated severe gusts and perhaps a 1-inch hail report or brief tornado remain possible over the next few hours across portions of the Ohio Valley. A Severe Thunderstorm Watch issuance remains possible if storms appear to increase in coverage and intensity.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Semi-discrete and small, linear storm structures have been pulsing in intensity across portions of the Ohio Valley ahead of the surface low track, where deep-layer ascent is greatest and where some surface-based buoyancy has been able to materialize given modest insolation. The primary limiting factor to a more widespread and robust severe threat continues to be mediocre low-level moisture. A narrow tongue of mid to upper 50s surface dewpoints continue to advect northward, immediately ahead of a semi-discrete supercell over Marshall County, KY, and this narrow corridor appears to be the most likely area to experience severe weather. HPX and LVX VWPs depict an eastward shift of the low-level jet axis. These VWPs show modestly curved hodographs in the 0-3 km layer, with 20Z RAP forecast soundings showing over 200 m2/s2 effective SRH given around 500 J/kg MLCAPE fueled by the narrow corridor of higher dewpoints. The main question is how long can the low-level moisture axis translate eastward in tandem with the storms. In the near term, any storms interacting with the low-level moisture may produce damaging gusts, and perhaps an instance of severe hail or a brief tornado. However, the severe threat is expected to be quite limited outside of the moisture axis. A Severe Thunderstorm Watch may be considered if confidence increases in the ongoing storms progressing through a longer-term moister environment.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Brief tornadoes remains possible with the stronger QLCS circulations over the next hour or so. A WW issuance is not expected given the isolated nature of the severe threat.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A QLCS has recently become organized over the past hour, with at least two different circulations being associated with TDSs. Current KLVX and TSDF radars show organized low-level circulations in progress. As long as these circulations persist, a brief tornado remains possible. However, 03Z mesoanalysis shows MLCAPE decreasing below 250 J/kg as MLCINH continues to increase. In addition, hodographs have increased in size farther east per ILN and JKL VWPs, suggesting that the low-level jet and resultant better low-level shear has also become eastward-displaced. As such, the ongoing tornado threat is expected to remain relatively isolated and short-lived, and a WW issuance is not currently expected.
